cls: Antidiabetic - sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor (prodrug, remogliflozin etabonate)
pharm: An oral SGLT2 inhibitor prodrug that increases urinary glucose excretion to lower blood glucose in type 2 diabetes; marketed in India, not FDA-approved
quick: Can be taken with or without food
Efficacy depends on renal function; avoid/limited use in significant impairment
Use with caution; data limited in severe impairment
Limit - increases hypoglycaemia and ketoacidosis risk
Glucose/HbA1c, renal function, volume status, genital infections, ketones if unwell
summary: Remogliflozin etabonate is an oral sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor prodrug used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus. After absorption it is rapidly converted to its active form, remogliflozin, which blocks SGLT2 in the proximal renal tubule, reducing glucose reabsorption and increasing urinary glucose excretion to lower plasma glucose in an insulin-independent manner. It is marketed in India (e.g. as Remo/Remozen) at a dose of 100 mg twice daily and is NOT FDA-approved, so this monograph is based on the India SmPC/prescribing information and SGLT2-inhibitor class data. As a class, SGLT2 inhibitors can cause genital mycotic and urinary infections, volume depletion and hypotension, and a risk of diabetic (including euglycaemic) ketoacidosis; efficacy depends on adequate renal function. Hypoglycaemia is uncommon as monotherapy but increases when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas.
indications: Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus, as an adjunct to diet and exercise, alone or in combination with other antidiabetic agents (India-approved indication)

dosage.n: India-approved dose; not an FDA-approved regimen

dosage.d: Avoid initiation or expect reduced efficacy when renal function is significantly reduced

admin: Take orally twice daily, with or without food
Assess renal function before starting and periodically; efficacy falls with declining eGFR
Ensure adequate hydration; counsel on volume depletion, especially with diuretics or in the elderly
Counsel on genital and urinary hygiene to reduce infection risk
Educate patients to recognise ketoacidosis symptoms and to seek care, even if blood glucose is near normal (euglycaemic DKA)
moa: Remogliflozin etabonate is a prodrug rapidly hydrolysed to the active moiety remogliflozin, a selective inhibitor of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) in the early proximal renal tubule. SGLT2 mediates the majority of filtered glucose reabsorption; its inhibition lowers the renal threshold for glucose and increases urinary glucose excretion, thereby reducing plasma glucose independently of insulin secretion or action. The accompanying osmotic diuresis and caloric loss can produce modest reductions in blood pressure and body weight.

absolute: Type 1 diabetes mellitus and diabetic ketoacidosis
Severe renal impairment, end-stage renal disease or dialysis (lack of efficacy)
relative: Volume-depleted patients or those on loop diuretics
History of recurrent genital or urinary infections
Conditions predisposing to ketoacidosis (low carbohydrate intake, acute illness, surgery, alcohol excess)
monitor: Renal function (eGFR) and volume status/blood pressure
Ketones if unwell or symptoms of acidosis

preg: There are no adequate data on remogliflozin in pregnancy and SGLT2 inhibitors as a class are not recommended during pregnancy (animal data show adverse renal development in the second and third trimesters). Avoid use in pregnancy and use alternative glucose-lowering therapy.
lact: It is not known whether remogliflozin is excreted in human milk; SGLT2 inhibitors are not recommended during breastfeeding because of potential effects on the developing kidney. Avoid use while breastfeeding.
renal: The glucose-lowering effect of remogliflozin depends on renal function and diminishes as eGFR falls. It is not recommended in significant renal impairment or end-stage renal disease. Assess renal function before and periodically during treatment.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; data in moderate-to-severe impairment are limited. Follow the prescribing information for dosing in liver disease.

moderate: Insulin and insulin secretagogues (sulfonylureas) - increased risk of hypoglycaemia; consider dose reduction of these agents
Diuretics - additive volume depletion and hypotension
interactions.food: Can be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol - increases risk of hypoglycaemia and of ketoacidosis
interactions.diagnostics: Causes glucosuria, so urine glucose tests are unreliable for monitoring; 1,5-anhydroglucitol assays are also affected

serious: Volume depletion with hypotension and acute kidney injury
Hypoglycaemia when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas
rare: Necrotising fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier gangrene) - SGLT2-class risk
emergency: Diabetic/euglycaemic ketoacidosis (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, breathlessness)
Severe dehydration with hypotension or acute kidney injury

monitoring: Blood glucose and HbA1c for glycaemic control
Renal function (eGFR) at baseline and periodically
Volume status and blood pressure, especially with diuretics or in the elderly
Blood ketones if the patient is unwell, vomiting or has abdominal pain
counsel: This medicine lowers blood sugar by making you pass extra glucose in the urine; take it twice a day
Drink enough fluids and report dizziness on standing, which can mean dehydration
Maintain good genital hygiene; report itching, discharge or pain on passing urine, as infections are more likely
Seek urgent care if you have nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or breathlessness, even if your sugar is not high (a serious acid build-up can occur)
Limit alcohol and tell your doctor before any surgery or if you become acutely ill, as the drug may need to be paused
pk: Glucosuria begins soon after dosing; glycaemic effect over days to weeks
Active remogliflozin reached rapidly after oral prodrug administration
Short - active remogliflozin half-life on the order of a few hours (supports twice-daily dosing)
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from moisture, per product label
pearls: NOTE: Remogliflozin etabonate is NOT FDA-approved; it is marketed in India - this monograph is based on the India SmPC/prescribing information and SGLT2-inhibitor class data
It is a prodrug rapidly converted to active remogliflozin; short half-life means twice-daily dosing (100 mg BID)
SGLT2-class risks: genital/urinary infections, volume depletion, and diabetic ketoacidosis including euglycaemic DKA
Glucose-lowering efficacy depends on renal function - avoid in significant renal impairment
Hypoglycaemia is uncommon alone but rises with insulin or sulfonylureas - reduce those doses
Counsel about pausing during acute illness/surgery and recognising Fournier gangrene of the perineum
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume your usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited; expected effects relate to excessive glucosuria and volume depletion. There is no specific antidote. Manage supportively with rehydration and monitoring of glucose, electrolytes and renal function; watch for ketoacidosis and treat hypoglycaemia if it occurs.
